No unresolved assumption changes the outcome; I accept no residual risk.

I examined the existing conclusion lock and the new currency branch at review_conclusions.go:418-464, 547-563. The new path adds no concurrent worker or cancellation lifecycle; the refusal returns before publishing a conclusion record, and the focused conclusion/provenance tests passed.

I examined the CLI/MCP conclusion path and the documented typed conclusion contract. The API shape and stored record format are unchanged; only non-approving runs may conclude over local edits, and an approval still requires current currency.

I examined reviewConclusionChecks and the draft parser/error paths at review_conclusions.go:91-148, 547-563. Invalid or incomplete run records remain refused; a currency-only approval refusal returns explicit reasons and does not publish.
I examined the shared conclusion writer and attestation preflight integration. The change reuses the existing proof and attestation boundary; it adds no provider, consumer or MCP schema.

I examined the refusal reasons at review_conclusions.go:137-148, 551-563. A currency-only refusal identifies the stale subject and tells the operator to retry after restoring the bundle materialization; no sensitive data is added.

I examined the public conclude behavior and compatibility documentation. Existing approval behavior and record schemas remain intact; callers gain a non-recorded refusal only for a stale approval, while older run briefs retain versioned verification.

The focused Go command passed. I examined the decision split at review_conclusions.go:125-148, 547-563, proof context at review_run_provenance.go:762-786, and current-bundle admission at review_bundle.go:3158-3173.

The design assessment observed no structural deltas. D1 implements R1-R2 with the smallest relevant split: a run record and its original brief establish a non-approval, while current bundle currency gates an approval. I examined review_conclusions.go:121-148 and review_run_provenance.go:762-774.

I examined the English and pt-BR manuals and both scaffold copies. Each describes the non-approving local-edit behavior, the approval retry condition and the preserved bundle binding consistently with runtime.

I examined the returned currency refusal at review_conclusions.go:551-563. It explains that no conclusion was recorded and gives a direct recovery action: make the working tree hold the bundle subject and conclude the same run again.

The focused regression command passed. TestARequestForChangesConcludesOverLocalEdits and TestAnApprovalOverLocalEditsIsNotRecordedAndConcludesLater cover R1-R3 in review_conclusion_local_edits_test.go:41-83; proof, bundle and verdict paths preserve D1.

I examined all eight sealed subject entries and the implementation. The changes are limited to review conclusion/provenance behavior, regression coverage and the four mirrored manuals; I found no unrelated behavior expansion.

I examined reviewRunRecordStands and proof verification. A non-approving run remains bound to its recorded bundle, transcript and output; changing its verdict would invalidate the proof, and attestation verification rejects any decision that differs from the run draft. No new authority or input path is introduced.

I examined D1 and the currency gates at review_conclusions.go:137-148, 551-563. The smallest sufficient choice is to keep run integrity checks universal and apply current-subject checks only to approvals. Always skipping currency could approve stale work; retaining it for all verdicts causes the reported refusal. This choice would be invalidated if a non-approving run could be transformed into an approval or if closeout accepted its old bundle.
